text:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] p99 latency spike detected for streaming endpoints — service=streaming, region=us-west-2. p99 jumped to 3.2s; p95 climbed to 700ms. Error budget burn increasing. Auto-mitigation not triggered.

elaine: seeing this on dashboards too. sudden increase in cache miss rate for prefix cache (~18% -> 67%). likely correlated with the prefix-hash rollout at ~2817498000.

sanjay: confirmed. I can repro higher tail on a few traces. stack shows frequent backpressure on paging worker and repeated KV lookups.

morgan: metrics dump snippet:```
streaming.p99=3.2s
streaming.p95=720ms
prefix_cache.hit_rate=33%
prefix_cache.miss_rate=67%
kv_latency.p99=120ms
request.retries=1.8%
```

arjun: any recent deploys besides the prefix hash? deploy-bot rolled new kernel optimizations earlier but that was healthy. deploy-bot: commit abc123 applied to prefix-service at 2817498100. rollout %100.

elaine: can we toggle to the previous hashing scheme? quick rollback of the prefix-hash rollout. if we revert, we should see hit rate recover and tail latency drop.

morgan: I'll try a scoped rollback on a subset (canary) first to validate. command I'll use:```bash
# rollback prefix-hash service to v0.9
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/prefix-service prefix-service=redwood/prefix-service:v0.9
```

arjun: ops-bot, start a throttling/routing policy to divert traffic to a lower-cost-but-more-stable model-variant for streaming traffic while we investigate. reduce concurrent streams per pod to prevent queuing.

ops-bot: acknowledged. applying rate-limits and routing rules now. expected to take effect ~90s.

elaine: customer-impact: looks like some long-polling customers may see delayed event delivery ~3-4s. alex-cs can you surface to top affected accounts, give them a note? mark P2 pending SLA impact assessment.

alex-cs: pinged top 6 accounts (IDs: C-731, C-412, C-999) with a heads-up. no escalations yet but some increased error logs in their apps. will keep them updated.

morgan: canaries rolled back at 2817500500 — prefix_cache.hit_rate on canary nodes climbed from 31% -> 78% within 2 minutes. p99 on canary pods dropped to 420ms.

sanjay: that's promising. runbook check: if canary improves, do full rollback. watch for KV blowback (too many warms). use 10% step increments.

elaine: proceeding with staged rollback now: steps: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%. watching hit-rate and p99 at each step. please don't apply any other hash-related changes meanwhile.

deploy-bot: full rollback to prefix-service:v0.9 completed at 2817503200 (user=morgan).

morgan: metrics after full rollback:```
prefix_cache.hit_rate=81%
streaming.p95=240ms
streaming.p99=380ms
kv_latency.p99=45ms
request.retries=0.2%
```

arjun: looks stable. Recommend keeping rollback in place until we can root-cause the hashing tweak and load-pattern interactions. opening a follow-up RFC for a careful re-rollout with additional cache-simulation tests.

elaine: good. next steps for oncall handoff: I'll be handing off at 2817507000 to sanjay for the overnight watch. summary for handoff below.

elaine: HANDOFF SUMMARY:
- Incident: streaming tail latency spike tied to prefix-hash rollout
- Mitigation: staged rollback to v0.9 completed, hit-rate & p95/p99 recovered
- Customer impact: transient increased latencies and some retries; CS notified top accounts; no formal SLA breach yet but close to p99 budget earlier
- Follow-ups: reproduce locally with synthetic workload, add cache warmup during rollouts, add preflight cache-hit simulation in CI, coordinate with model-routing to avoid concurrent heavy KV warming during deploys

elaine: logs/commands used during triage attached here for next oncall:```bash
# health checks
curl -s https://metrics.internal/api/streaming?window=5m | jq '.p99, .p95'
# rollback
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/prefix-service prefix-service=redwood/prefix-service:v0.9
# check cache metrics
curl -s https://metrics.internal/api/cache/prefix | jq '.hit_rate, .miss_rate'
```

sanjay: taking watch. key things on my radar: keep an eye on prefix_cache.hit_rate for >75% and streaming.p99 < 500ms. if we see kv_latency spike >150ms do immediate rate-limit. contact oncall infra if KV cluster nodes appear overloaded.

ops-bot: incident ticket INC-2026-482 created and linked. severity P2. runbook assigned to elaine and sanjay.

alex-cs: shared note with customers: "We're investigating intermittent streaming delays. We have implemented mitigations and are monitoring; we'll update in 1 hour or sooner."

morgan: creating post-incident task list: 1) validate prefix hashing logic with larger key distribution tests 2) implement rollout job that warms cache incrementally 3) add synthetic traffic test in staging that simulates hot prefixes 4) update rollout playbook to include immediate rollback threshold at >40% cache miss increase.

elaine: thanks all. closing live incident channel for now — will reopen if things regress. keep updates brief on-watch. :white_check_mark:
